name: Question 1
problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{2}}{4}+18,\,\frac{(2t-1)(t+8)}{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{2}}{4}+18),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{(2t-1)(t+8)}{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{2\cdot (t+8)+(2t-1)\cdot 1}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{4t+15}{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4t+15}{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨t24+18,(2t−1)(t+8)4⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨12,1⟩
b
a=⟨t2,t⟩
c
a=⟨12,t4⟩
d
a=⟨1,1⟩
e
a=⟨t2,t−14⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(t24+18),ddt((2t−1)(t+8)4)⟩=⟨t2,2⋅(t+8)+(2t−1)⋅14⟩=⟨t2,4t+154⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(4t+154)⟩=⟨12,1⟩
